summary.text: 你 means “you,” usually addressing one person. Its visible form combines 亻, the person-category element in one proposed analysis, and 尔, the simplified form of 爾, which was also used for “you/your.” The competing construction analyses remain unresolved; the proposed sound role of 尔 is not established by the modern readings alone.

formation.text: A plausible analysis is phonosemantic: 亻 supplies the person category and 尔 a sound cue. A competing account reads 人 and 尔 together as “person” and “you.” The construction remains disputed because the available historical accounts do not directly establish how 你 was formed.

components.text: In one proposed phonosemantic analysis, 亻 represents a person and contributes the semantic category. The available evidence does not establish that role historically.

The right-side 尔 is proposed as the phonetic element. It is the standardized simplified form of 爾; 爾 was used for ‘you/your,’ and 尔 is described as its shortened form. This graphic and word history does not prove 尔’s sound role in 你.

sound_limitation.text: The modern Mandarin readings ěr and nǐ can be compared, and one supplied secondary account gives Old Chinese *njelʔ for 尔 and *nɯʔ for 你. Those reconstructions are not an independently verified matched comparison here and do not establish 尔’s historical phonetic role in 你.

sound.text: In modern Mandarin, 尔 is ěr and 你 is nǐ. This comparison alone does not demonstrate the proposed historical sound relationship.

history.text: The dictionaries report 你 glossed as “you” in 集韻 and cite its use in 隋書. The earliest surviving written example and the date of the quoted wording remain unresolved. A small-seal-style rendering of 你 is a modern font construction, not an ancient form.

The reported graphic account describes 尔 as taking the upper part of 爾. Separately, 尔/爾 was used for “you/your.” This history of 尔 neither establishes that it depicts an object nor explains its proposed sound function in 你.

uncertainties.text: The phonosemantic and ideographic analyses of 你 are both reported, but no supplied historical account directly establishes its construction. The proposed sound analysis should therefore be treated as plausible, not certain.
No original depicted object or independently recoverable object-name pronunciation for 尔 is established, so an account of 你 as a borrowing from an object-name is unsupported.

Bare 你 is recorded in plural examples from historical works, while ordinary modern plural usage is documented in 你们. The cited evidence does not establish the present-day frequency or productivity of bare-你 plural use, or a dated semantic link from singular ‘you’.

senses.period: Current Mandarin use; historical examples are cited in 集韻 and other works
senses.text: 你 is the ordinary second-person pronoun meaning “you,” usually singular in present-day Mandarin. Dictionaries cite the gloss 汝也 (“you”) and historical second-person examples; these do not establish the exact earliest surviving occurrence or date the wording of the quoted passages.

senses.period: attested in cited historical examples; present-day status unresolved
senses.text: A character dictionary records bare 你 in plural examples such as 你兩個 (‘you two’) and 你眾人 (‘you all’). These cited examples are from historical works; their frequency or productivity in present-day speech is not established here. This is distinct from the ordinary modern plural construction 你们, formed from singular pronoun 你 with 们.

limitations.text: The evidence does not establish when the dictionary-recorded bare-你 plural examples arose, whether that use remains current or productive, or a semantic development linking it to the singular pronoun. The ordinary modern plural construction 你们 is separately documented.

relationships.text: One reported analysis assigns 亻 a semantic role, while another treats 人 and 尔 ideographically. The supplied evidence does not establish 亻’s historical role in 你.

One analysis proposes 尔 as the sound element. The modern Mandarin readings are ěr and nǐ, but the supplied evidence does not establish a historical sound relation; another analysis treats the parts ideographically.

overview.text: 你 means “you,” usually addressing one person. Its visible parts are 亻, treated as the person-category element in one proposed analysis, and 尔, the simplified form of 爾, also used for “you/your.” The formation remains disputed.

components.text: One analysis treats 亻 as the person category; its historical role in 你 remains unresolved.
尔 is proposed as a sound cue, but its role in 你 is not established.

limitations.text: No verified historical image of 你 is available here: the proposed small-seal-style image is a modern font construction, and the available 尔 glyph images do not have verified reuse terms. The reported relationship between 尔 and 爾 does not establish an attested early form of the full character 你.
